Az MTI arról írt, hogy a jogszabályt még 2025-ben kezdeményezte a nemrég meghalt Lindsey Graham , aki elkötelezett támogatója volt Ukrajnának. A Graham nevét viselő törvényt kétpárti támogatással fogadta el a szenátus, vagyis az amerikai parlament, a Kongresszus felsőháza. A végszavazás várhatóan szeptember elején lesz, ekkor kerül majd a törvény a képviselőház elé. A törvény másodlagos vámokról szóló része főleg az orosz energiahordozók legnagyobb vásárlóit, vagyis Indiát és Kínát érinti, de az európai vásárlókra, így Magyarországra is hatással lehet. Igaz, a törvény alól Donald Trump személyesen felmentést adhat, és a jogszabályban meghatározott intézkedések hatálya azonnal megszűnik, ha békét vagy tűzszünetet köt egymással Oroszország és Ukrajna. Éjszaka orosz rakéta- és dróntámadás ért 12 ukrajnai régiót, 13 ember meghalt, 77-en pedig megsebesültek – mondta Volodimir Zelenszkij a belgrádi sajtótájékoztatóján. Arról beszélt, hogy országszerte késtek a vonatok, mert az orosz hadsereg energetikai létesítményeket és a vasúti infrastruktúrát is támadta. Timur Tkacsenko, Kijev katonai közigazgatásának vezetője azt mondta, az ukrán főváros közelében az orosz támadásokban éjszaka legalább hárman meghaltak , köztük egy gyerek – írta a BBC. https://www.theguardian.com/australia-ne.text: Pauline Hanson says she is opposed to a major gun buyback being announced by Anthony Albanese and the NSW premier, Chris Minns, in Sydney shortly. Legislation for the plan passed parliament earlier this year, part of the response to the Bondi beach terror attack. It will be run in two phases, with the cost split 50:50 between the federal and NSW governments. Under the first phase of the scheme, $1,000 will be paid for revolvers and $850 for semi-automatic handguns. Compensation of $850 will be paid for double-barrel shotguns and $650 for those with a single barrel. Between $650 and $1,000 will be paid for rifles, while air rifles have a fixed compensation of $450. Hanson told News24 taxpayers should not pay for the scheme. She suggested the buyback would impact “law-abiding Australians who are trying to go about their business, like farmers that need their guns,” she said. https://www.worcesternews.co.uk/news/265.text: River Severn West Mercia Police Crime Emergency Worcestershire Worcester Men fishing in River Severn made 'threatening gestures' at pensioner By Mary Stenson Reporter Share 0 Comments 3 Skip to next photo 1 / 1 Show caption 1 / 1 Share 0 Comments This article is brought to you by our exclusive subscriber partnership with our sister title USA Today, and has been written by our American colleagues. It does not necessarily reflect the view of The Herald. A PENSIONER said he was "disgusted" after a group of men fishing in the river made threatening gestures at him. Paul Smith said he was walking near the River Severn in Worcester on Thursday afternoon (September 3) when he noticed the group of men on a boat fishing in the swan sanctuary area. He said he called out to the group to inform them that fishing is prohibited in this area, a rule that is made clear by signs on railings in the area. READ NEXT: Polish community's heartbreak and deep shock after Worcester murder 'They weren't joking' The 69-year-old said the men became threatening, making throat-slicing and punching gestures. He said they also started threatening to beat him up when they got off the boat. "They weren’t joking," Mr Smith said. "I was disgusted because they didn’t seem to give a damn about the rules about the swans. "I was apprehensive because I didn’t know if they were carrying knives or anything." BAN: Fishing is prohibited in the swan sanctuary area of the River Severn (Image: Supplied) As directed by the 'no fishing' sign, he called police on 101, and said he also reported the men's threatening behaviour. Mr Smith said he also made the call handler aware that he was being threatened. READ NEXT: Worcester optician keeps door locked while shop is open after thefts elsewhere Disappointed by police response He made the call at 1.03pm and was on the phone for several minutes. After 45 minutes, he left the area when police still hadn't arrived. West Mercia Police has confirmed that officers attended the scene at 2.07pm. "I waited 45 minutes for police," Mr Smith said. "They never turned up. I even tried to flag a police car down." INCIDENT: Paul Smith said he was 'disgusted' by the men's actions and 'disappointed' in the police response (Image: NQ) The force said the call was deemed 'Grade 2', meaning officers should attend within two hours. When they did arrive, officers spoke to "potential witnesses" but no suspects have been found. "Officers received reports of anti-social behaviour and illegal fishing on the River Severn yesterday, shortly after 1pm yesterday," a West Mercia Police spokesperson said. "All incidents reported to us are assessed according to the level of risk and harm they present to the public, this ensures our resources are directed the quickest to those who need them the most. "This incident was assessed as a Grade 2 response, requiring attendance within two hours. "Officers arrived at the location within one hour of the report being received, carried out a search and spoke to a number of potential witnesses. "No arrests have been made in connection to the matter. "Anyone who wishes to report anti-social behaviour is advised to contact their local safer neighbourhood team." https://www.euronews.com/2026/11/27/russ.text: Since the evening of Thursday 26 November, Russian forces have attacked Ukraine with 155 strike UAVs of various types (51 of them jet powered), as well as Parodiya-type decoy drones. Ukrainian air defences managed to shoot down (source in Ukrainian) 110 drones, but impacts were recorded at several locations.Prime Minister Sergey Koretsky said that during the night the Russian Armed Forces carried out strikes on civilian infrastructure in nine regions of Ukraine."Tonight Russia carried out strikes on the railway, the energy sector, civilian enterprises and residential buildings in nine regions," he wrote (source in Ukrainian) on Telegram.As a result of the Russian attacks, by morning part of consumers in Dnipropetrovsk, Zaporizhzhia, Kirovohrad, Sumy, Kharkiv and Kherson regions were left without electricity, according to Ukraine's First Deputy Energy Minister Artem Nekrasov.In particular, he said (source in Ukrainian) that in Dnipropetrovsk region engineers have been forced to carry out emergency shutdowns because equipment has been damaged and voltage has fallen in the high-voltage grid.According to the authors of the November economic overview (source in Ukrainian) by the Centre for Economic Strategy (CES), after the Russian attack on 20 November Ukraine completely halted electricity exports, and imports reached their highest level since mid-June.Since September, Russia has carried out more than 1,000 strikes on Ukraine's energy system, targeting not only generation facilities but also high-voltage substations through which electricity reaches consumers.As a result of the overnight strikes, two people were killed at an enterprise in Nizhyn in Chernihiv region; people may be trapped under the rubble.One woman, aged 86, was killed and another six people were injured after Russian Armed Forces attacks on Izium in the Kharkiv region. Blocks of flats and private houses, administrative buildings and vehicles were damaged, and fires broke out in various parts of the city.One person was killed in Kryvyi Rih and another two were wounded after more than 20 UAV strikes on five districts of the Dnipropetrovsk region.Three people were injured on the morning of 27 November as a result of strikes by Russian drones on the Shevchenkivskyi and Kyiv districts of Kharkiv.Strike by Ukrainian forces on chemical plant producing fuel for Iskander missilesOn Friday night Ukrainian drones struck a combined heat and power plant that is part of the Rosatom state corporation, as well as a synthetic rubber plant involved in producing components of solid rocket fuel, in Yefremov in the Tula region.This is at least the third strike on the chemical complex over the past year.It produces polymers for the rubber industry, electrical engineering, adhesives, sealants and lubricants, as part of the enterprise's output is dual-use.In September the General Staff of the Ukrainian Armed Forces claimed (source in Ukrainian) that the Yefremov plant is involved in producing components of solid rocket fuel, including for ballistic missiles of the Iskander operational-tactical complexes. The plant has been under Ukrainian sanctions since May 2023.Also overnight there were reports (source in Russian) of a massive drone attack on Saint Petersburg and Leningrad region. The authorities of the northern city said that 45 drones had been shot down over the region. In Novorossiysk three people were injured in a drone attack, the operational headquarters of Krasnodar region reported. Another two people were killed in Bryansk region by a drone strike and an explosive device that was dropped.The Russian Defence Ministry reported that 318 Ukrainian UAVs had been shot down in 10 regions, as well as over illegally annexed Crimea.Ukrainian troops also reported (source in Ukrainian) destroying a camouflaged oil depot in occupied territory in Luhansk region, which Russian forces were using to supply fuel to their units.Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky summed up the impact of Ukrainian strikes on Russian refineries and defence industry facilities, saying there were "results" in Samara, Nizhny Novgorod, Krasnodar, Rostov, Volgograd, Stavropol, Bryansk, Perm and Tula regions, as well as in Bashkortostan and Tatarstan, and in the Black Sea."Ukraine is absolutely right to respond to every Russian strike. And I thank our Ukrainian defence forces for ensuring that the responses are accurate.""Russian oil facilities, enterprises involved in producing explosives and other sites that serve the needs of the war, military airfields and aircraft, our range covers all of this," the president said.
